chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to me from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim from his father from Ismail ibn Marrar from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who gives ghusl to a body of a believer and remains trustworthy with him, Allah will forgive [his sins].
And how should one be trustworthy with him? He said: He should not tell others what he sees.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Allah's forgiveness when giving ghusl to a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq emphasizes that the spiritual reward for performing the ritual bath (ghusl) is contingent upon maintaining 'al-amanah' (trustworthiness), specifically by concealing any physical defects or private matters observed on the deceased. This principle of guarding the deceased's dignity mirrors the broader Islamic ethic of 'satr' (concealment of faults), ensuring that the act of service does not become a source of embarrassment for the departed. It highlights the intimate connection between the physical care of the body and the spiritual preservation of its honor.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali Majluwayh from Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim from his father from Ismail b. Marrar from Yunis b. Abdulrahman from Abdillah b. Sinan from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who gives ghusl to a body of a believer and remain trustworthy with him, Allah will forgive all his sins.”
Someone asked, “How should one be trustworthy?” Imam (a.s.) answered, “One should not tell to others what he sees on the body.”
